brief_summary: A meal rich in very-long chain omega-3 fatty acids or oleic acid may lower postprandial insulin levels in comparison to a meal rich in linoleic acid or palmitic acid. A meal rich in very long-chain omega-3 fatty acids may lower postprandial triglyceride levels compared to other fatty acids.
brief_title: Lipid, Glycemic, and Insulin Responses to Meals Rich in Different Fatty Acids

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Type 2 diabetes mellitus not on insulin therapy

Exclusion Criteria:

* Thyroid, renal, or hepatic disease, uncontrolled hypertension, anemia, history of ketosis

interventions.name: Test meals rich in different fatty acids

lead_sponsor.name: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

official_title: Lipid, Glycemic, and Insulin Responses to Meals Rich in Saturated, Cis-Monounsaturated, and Polyunsaturated Fatty (n-3 and n-6)Acids in Subjects With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

sites.facility: UT Southwestern Medical Center at Dallas
